name: rates
title: Conversion Rates
description: What one denomination was worth in another, at a moment, according to a named source. Append-only, because a rate is a historical observation and not a settable value: if a source restates, that is a NEW row with a later fetched_at, never an edit to what we recorded at the time (docs/logic-decisions.md #3 and #8 -- rates come from outside, so they get the same evidence posture as bank statements). Rates exist for two jobs and no others: supplying the rate a transaction STAMPS on itself when it happens (#1 -- history is never re-derived from today's price), and revaluing balances at a period end. They are deliberately not a tick database: store what you stamp, plus the closes and averages a period needs. `kind` matters more than most systems admit -- accounting standards use different rates for different purposes (the transaction rate when it happened, the closing rate for revaluing monetary balances, an average rate for translating a period's activity, and the historical rate that non-monetary items keep forever), and a system that offers only one number quietly picks the wrong one somewhere. The rate itself is stored as an exact decimal STRING rather than integer minor units, because unlike money it is a measurement with significant figures, not a count of things -- what must be exact is the converted result, which object_money.convert() produces as whole minor units with the rounding made explicit.

fields.name: quote_code
fields.label: Quote
fields.help: The denomination it is priced in (USD in 'BTC/USD = 67432.10').

fields.name: rate
fields.label: Rate
fields.help: How many quote units one base unit is worth, as an exact decimal string with as many digits as the source gave. Never a float.

fields.name: as_of
fields.label: As Of
fields.help: The moment this rate describes -- not when it was fetched. A lookup never uses a rate dated after the transaction it is valuing.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Kind
fields.help: spot: the price at a moment (what a transaction stamps). close: an official end-of-period price (what revaluation uses). average: a period average (what translating a period's activity uses). historical: a rate deliberately frozen to an original transaction, for items that are never revalued.

fields.name: period
fields.label: Period
fields.help: For close/average rates, the period they belong to: 2026-07 or 2026-07-24. Blank for spot.

fields.name: source
fields.label: Source
fields.help: Who said so (coinbase, ecb, manual). Part of the rate's identity: two sources disagreeing is normal and must not be silently averaged.

fields.name: fetched_at
fields.label: Fetched
fields.help: When we recorded it, as distinct from the moment it describes. A restatement is a new row with a later fetched_at.
